dialect.guess: IBM Enterprise COBOL or compatible (likely GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL given JMA ORCA open-source context)
evidence: IDENTIFICATION DIVISION / ENVIRONMENT DIVISION / DATA DIVISION / PROCEDURE DIVISION all present
SELECT ... ASSIGN ... ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED ... ACCESS MODE IS DYNAMIC ... RECORD KEY ... FILE STATUS

purpose.summary: This program is part of the JMA (Japan Medical Association) ORCA open-source medical receipt (claims) software. It generates a monthly statistical report (CSV output) of medical procedures by category (診療行為別集計表 – medical-act-by-category aggregation table), reading indexed files of procedure activity and accounting data and writing CSV output.
purpose.domain: healthcare / medical billing (Japanese national health insurance claims processing)

notable_features: No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS – pure file-based batch processing
Multiple COPY statements with REPLACING (copybook-driven data structures)
Indexed sequential file I/O with DYNAMIC access mode
Japanese Shift-JIS / EUC-JP encoded comments and data literals (decoded as latin-1, causing mojibake in display)
CSV output generation with Japanese column headers embedded as VALUE literals
OCCURS tables for procedure category codes and patient information
REDEFINES used to overlay table structure over flat value area
21 CALL statements indicating modular subprogram architecture
137 PERFORM statements indicating structured procedural decomposition
Error file (RECEERR-FILE) for logging processing errors
verdict.notes: File decoded with latin-1 but contains Japanese multi-byte characters (EUC-JP or Shift-JIS), causing garbled display of comments and string literals. The program is clearly part of the well-known JMA ORCA open-source medical receipt system, a production-grade Japanese healthcare application. The COPY statements reference external copybooks (CPSRYACCT.INC, COMMON-SPA, CPCOMMONDAT2.INC, CPRECEERR.INC, HCG017.INC, CPPTINF.INC) that are not included in this file. Version history comments indicate active maintenance from 2006 through 2019.
